messages:
maria: Quick perf note — ran a cross-GPU sweep for continuous batching. Varied max_tokens_per_batch = [512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192] across A10 / T4 / L4 / A100 / H100. Observed odd regression on A10: p99 +10-15% when max_tokens >= 4096, and profiler shows kernel fallback + increased KV cache fragmentation. Dropping raw profiler snippets below.

bench-bot: profiler summary (model=x42, seq_len=64, continuous-batching enabled):
```
A100 | max_tokens=8192 -> throughput=20.1k tokens/s, p99=42ms, kv_hit=0.95, kernel=v2_fused
H100 | max_tokens=8192 -> throughput=26.3k tokens/s, p99=33ms, kv_hit=0.96, kernel=v3_opt
L4   | max_tokens=4096 -> throughput=9.8k tokens/s,  p99=78ms, kv_hit=0.88, kernel=v2_fused
A10  | max_tokens=4096 -> throughput=6.3k tokens/s,  p99=120ms, kv_hit=0.70, kernel=fallback_scalar (lots of mem copies)
T4   | max_tokens=2048 -> throughput=5.9k tokens/s,  p99=150ms, kv_hit=0.65, kernel=legacy
```
(bench-bot: numbers are aggregate from 10 runs; kv_hit = prefix/KV cache hit ratio observed)

ashok: can you paste the exact runtime config and the queue policy used for the sweep? was batching_mode=continuous_default or did you use the new steady-fill policy?

maria: config used for sweep:
```
serving.runtime.batch.max_tokens_per_batch = sweep_value
serving.runtime.batch.min_batch_fill_ms = 6
serving.runtime.batch.max_batch_delay_ms = 12
serving.runtime.batch.mode = continuous_default
serve.kv.cache.enabled = true
serve.kv.cache.max_shards = 128
```
Also we used the default queue policy (priority by arrival, no seq_len bucketing).

tara: ok. initial hypothesis: A10's slower memory bandwidth + large max_tokens increases KV cache fragmentation (more small KV segments), causing extra memcpy and kernel path fallback. Two quick mitigations: 1) lower max_tokens cap for A10, 2) enable seq_len bucketing or stable-shape batching so kernel selector sees uniform shapes.

devon: kernel selector logs show: when batch contains >30% sequences with seq_len < 32 and the rest large, selector picks fallback_scalar because fused kernels require uniform tileable shapes. That explains the huge p99. We should try grouping by seq_len buckets and prefer fused kernels even if it delays batch formation slightly.

will: proposed per-gpu token_budget targets (for continuous-batching stable defaults):
- H100: 8192
- A100: 8192
- L4: 4096
- A10: 2048 (soft cap)
- T4: 1024 (soft cap)
These are soft caps; keep max batch count high but cap tokens to avoid large mixed-shape batches.

maria: tested quick patch: added token_budget cap only for A10 (2048) + seq_len bucketing (bins: 1-32,33-128,129-512). Re-ran 5 runs: A10 p99 dropped from 120ms -> 78ms, kv_hit improved 0.70 -> 0.82. No measurable regression on A100/H100.

ashok: nice. Did kernel selection logs indicate restored fused kernels?

maria: yes — fused kernel usage on A10 jumped from 22% -> 71% for those runs. Also memory copy counts dropped ~40%.

tara: sounds good. we should roll a conservative config change: apply per-GPU token_budget defaults and enable seq_len bucketing by default for continuous mode behind a feature flag. Also add an experiment to evaluate customer-level latency impact for low QPS traffic.

devon: one caveat: bucketing increases cold-starts for tiny buckets at very low QPS. Suggest a fallback policy when backlog < 3: ignore bucket and allow small mixed batch to avoid API latency regressions.

will: ack. Action items: 1) eng-runtime to ship token_budget defaults PR (maria+ashok) 2) enable seq_len bucketing feature flag + docs (devon) 3) telemetry: add metric kv_fragmentation_ratio and kernel_path_fraction per GPU (tara) 4) run canary across small set of Dedicated nodes (will).

maria: I'll open the PR with the patch and attach the microbench harness and raw outputs. Quick note: also saw T4 become erratic at max_tokens=2048 for long sequences — will schedule a T4-specific sweep next.

will: thanks — ping me when PR is up and I'll schedule canary. :thumbsup:
